chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

A man from the people of Khorasan entered upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who had dealt in usury until his wealth increased. Then he asked the jurists, and they said: 'Nothing will be accepted from you unless you return it to its owners.' So he came to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and recounted his story to him.

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Your way out is from the Book of Allah, Exalted and Glorified: "So whoever comes to him with a warning from his Lord and desists, then for him is what has already passed, and his affair is left to Allah." (1) And the warning is repentance.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on wealth acquired through usury according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) clarifies that the 'warning' (maw'izah) in the verse is specifically repentance (tawbah), offering a theological basis for retaining wealth after sincere repentance rather than strict restitution to specific owners. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between the general prohibition of riba and the practical resolution of accumulated wealth through divine mercy, contrasting with the stricter view of the jurists who demanded specific return.
